chapter: Bass, drums and the big-band rhythm section
title: Why bass horns gave way and rhythm sections of the great bands
summary: Bass horns were dropped as drummers toned down; rhythm sections of Ellington, Lunceford, Cab Calloway and Henderson compared.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: that; they had to have those contrasts. But to answer your question there, first I have to go back a little bit. Remember, in the early '30s or the late '20s, they started getting rid of the bass horns.
Right.

Now, first of all, most of them you couldn't disconnect. It was all one solid piece, like my bass horn would take up a whole truck bed. You couldn't unscrew that bell and fold it up into a compact little thing.
It was all one piece, was it?
Yeah. Three times as big as a bass fiddle.
Yeah.

Plus Pops Foster and those guys down in New Orleans had shown that it could be done if that drummer would come down a little bit. Now, with that big foot a bass fiddle could not be heard, so they had to start tonin' down. And if you'll listen at Duke's earlier records, Sonny Greer and them, with Wellman Braud, how splendid they sounded. Now Sonny still has a heavier foot than Jo Jones, but the way they blended in and they swung it was --it showed that that rhythm section was teaming.
Well, also, Wellman Braud --
Wellman Braud was strong.
You'd go right up to the mike.
Yeah, but don't forget now, before that time they didn't have a mike.
No.
When they came to those little towns, there wasn't no such thing as a mike.
That's it.
And you could hear them. I think of Lunceford when they came there, that bass player played mostly two-beat.
That was Moses Allen.
Moses Allen, right. He mostly played two-beat. But he cut through with ol' (Crawford) you know.
Yeah.
They blended. First of all, I say that no band was great unless they had a strong rhythm section.
Right.

They had to have a motor, y'know. Well, now, I'll go on. So the guys was doing; with they excepted from Duke, you didn't have too great a rhythm section with Cab, but he was quite a show, y'know. Now Fletcher didn't have too good a rhythm section. Moten had a--
Fletcher had, uh--
Arrangements.
